//: Story Phase 13: more sources, no more truth. Reliability: somehow worse.

variants.source: Garrick; the Cheap-O-Rama pocket booklet; the Stenchmaster Channel (sponsored by the Bling Bling King)
variants.evidence: None. Three sources, and every one of them is him, one way or another
variants.note: He's HERE. He's been on my ship all along, pretending to be Pete. (Captain.) / He has NOT. It's me. PETE. I've got a peg leg. Brogath didn't have a peg leg. (Pete, in the margin.)

variants.source: Garrick; the Cheap-O-Rama pocket booklet; the Stenchmaster Channel (sponsored by the Bling Bling King)
variants.evidence: None. Now on television. With a sponsor
variants.note: A special. Three minutes of digging, no sash holders, one blast, a storm of sharks wearing it. Brought to you by the shark that has OUR treasure. Being on television doesn't make it true. It makes it worse.

entries.title: The Stenchmaster Channel
entries.claim: Twenty-four hours a day of Ancient Stenchmaster history, narrated, now in Stench-O-Vision. Princess Stenchalina's First Grand Disaster (still running). Brogath: Poor in Gold, Rich in Gas.
entries.source: A Build-Your-Own S.E.S. kit (ages eight and up), a cable that goes round a cannon, and the Mark II's sauce can
entries.evidence: A television built out of a kit, three of Jim's forks, Sully's horseshoe, a copper coil and a transformer that hums
entries.verified: It's on television. That isn't the same thing
entries.note: The set has a smell vent. Nobody asked for a smell vent. I shut it. The smell that was already out stayed.

variants.evidence: A television programme, narrated, in Stench-O-Vision: the castle of onions, the First Royal Waft, the ribbon. A runtime clock in the corner that never stopped
variants.note: It's on the Channel now. The castle was made of ONIONS. Ned has been saying so for weeks. Nobody listened to Ned. The Disaster is still running, apparently. Somewhere. Very quietly.

entries.title: The Returned Pillow
entries.caption: NO THANKS. RETURN TO SENDER. TOO STINKY.
entries.printed: NO THANKS. RETURN TO SENDER. TOO STINKY. (On a participation medal, pinned through a pillow.)
entries.arrived: Thrown back over the port rail, twice: the second time precisely, at my feet

entries.title: The Smell Complaint
entries.caption: SMELL COMPLAINT: WHATEVER THAT IS, TURN IT OFF.
entries.printed: SMELL COMPLAINT: WHATEVER THAT IS, TURN IT OFF. - YOUR NEIGHBOURS (THE STORM). / NOISE COMPLAINT (AGAIN): THE HUMMING.
entries.arrived: Down the old quarters' ladder hatch, the moment the bedroom set started to smell
entries.verdict: Even the weather has standards. It's right, which is the worst part.

entries.title: The Campaign
entries.caption: VOTE CAPTAIN BROGATH FOR CAPTAIN!
entries.printed: VOTE CAPTAIN BROGATH FOR CAPTAIN! MORE SHARK TREASURE FOR EVERYONE! (TREASURE NOT GUARANTEED.) / STINKBEARD FOR CAPTAIN! NO FARTS! NO BROGATHS! NO FUN! / HOLD MY SASH: A HOSTILE TAKEOVER. / TONIGHT: THE GREAT BROGATH DEBATE. SPONSORED BY CHEAP-O-RAMA.
entries.arrived: On the binnacle and the deck, one per gust, while I held her steady
entries.verdict: There is no election. You don't elect a captain at sea, in a storm. (Pete.) It's campaigning anyway.

variants.notes: About nine hours left. He hasn't let a single one go. Five loopholes, all no. He came up the ladder in a burgundy suit and told me the truth about the treasure-room growl. I believed him, for a moment. The sash is still in my wardrobe. So is the song.

entries.title: The Old Quarters
entries.where: Below the galley, through the old door (and the fore hatch)
entries.notes: Opened. It growled. Judged, piled, thrown into the storm, sent back FOLDED. Locked in the linen locker and nailed shut: DO NOT OPEN. IT GROWLS. Remade in two hundred and ninety toy sashes. It looks like the inside of his head. Everybody sleeps better. I hate it.

variants.notes: Remade in toy sashes, and now a gift shop: pennants, mugs, a Bean Bailiff badge, and five cardboard Ancient Stenchmasters where I put them. A second television on the barrel table. It smells. (Not any more. I shut it.)

entries.title: Brogath (Sightings)
entries.where: In the old quarters. Wearing Pete.
entries.notes: I breathed it. Through my beard. All of it. Then I looked at Pete and Pete wasn't Pete. (Pete, in the margin: I AM PETE.)

variants.where: On deck (Pete). On deck (cardboard). In the treasure room (alleged, behind the door).
variants.notes: He touched the helm. I held her steady through three gusts and a campaign. The treasure-room growl, Garrick says, is his OLD fart, from the first night. I understood that. For a moment. Pete is still Brogath. (Pete, in the margin, very large: WHY DO WE KEEP LOSING PROGRESS?)

variants.where: On deck (Pete). On deck (cardboard). In the treasure room (behind the door).
variants.notes: There's one in the treasure room. Pete agrees: as long as the door stays shut, he can't blast the treasure away. But WHICH Brogath? (Pete, in the margin: there's NONE.)
Pete brought the cardboard one up to prove a point. So: the cardboard one is Pete, and Pete is Brogath. It makes sense. (Pete, in the margin: it makes the OPPOSITE of sense.)
